# AI Video Studio

> AI Video Studio is a free, open-source, local AI video generator for Windows, Linux and macOS.
> It turns a text script into a finished MP4 — narrated, scored, word-synced-captioned and
> colour-graded — entirely on the user's own GPU, with no cloud rendering, no API keys and no
> subscription. It is a self-hosted alternative to hosted text-to-video services such as Runway,
> Pika and Sora.

AI Video Studio is an Electron + React desktop application over a local FastAPI daemon. A text
script is refined into scene prompts by Gemma (served by Ollama), drawn as a character sheet and
per-scene keyframes by FLUX.1, animated into clips by Wan2.2 TI2V-5B through ComfyUI, smoothed to
48 fps by RIFE, narrated by Kokoro TTS, captioned word-by-word by faster-whisper, scored by
ACE-Step, and assembled by FFmpeg on NVENC. Every model stage runs on CUDA. Nothing leaves the
machine; there is no telemetry and no account.

Current version: 2.0.1. Version 2 replaced most of the v1 pipeline — Wan2.1 became Wan2.2
TI2V-5B, FLUX was added for character sheets and keyframes, the CPU `minterpolate` and `super2xbr`
paths were replaced by RIFE 4.9 and Real-ESRGAN on the GPU, and MusicGen was demoted to a fallback
behind ACE-Step because MusicGen's weights are CC-BY-NC.

Repository: https://github.com/06pratyush/ai-video-pipeline
Project site: https://06pratyush.github.io/ai-video-pipeline/

## Key facts

- **Licence:** MIT. Free permanently — no paid tier, no metering, no account, no telemetry.
- **Hardware:** NVIDIA GPU with 8 GB VRAM minimum (a laptop GPU is enough; the video model is a
  4-bit GGUF build), 12 GB or more recommended; 16 GB RAM (32 GB recommended); 45 GB free disk, of
  which the v2 model stack is about 34 GB (100 GB recommended). CPU-only mode is not practical for
  video in v2. AMD GPUs are not supported yet, because the GGUF video path has no tested ROCm
  build.
- **Render time:** set by the video model, not the application. Measured on an RTX 4060 Laptop
  (8 GB VRAM, 16 GB RAM): about **16 minutes** for a 2-scene project through the app's render
  queue, and about **2 h 35 min** for a 13-scene, 77-second film. v1 documentation claimed 5–15
  minutes per video; that figure was wrong by roughly an order of magnitude and does not describe
  this pipeline.
- **Verified platforms:** a full end-to-end render is verified on Windows on an RTX 4060 Laptop
  (8 GB VRAM, 16 GB RAM). Linux, macOS and GPUs below 8 GB are not yet verified — tracked as
  GAP-04 in CONTEXT.md.
- **Platforms:** Windows 10/11 (NSIS installer or portable .exe), Linux (AppImage or .deb),
  macOS 12+ (DMG for Apple Silicon or Intel).
- **Runtime:** Python 3.10+ (3.11 recommended) and Node.js 18 LTS+ (20 LTS recommended). The
  backend daemon binds to 127.0.0.1:7860 only and has no authentication by design.
- **Offline:** fully offline after the first-run setup and model download, apart from an optional
  update check against GitHub Releases.
- **Output rights:** the application code is MIT, but generated video is governed by the licences
  of the underlying models, which must be checked separately. Wan2.2, FLUX.1 schnell, ACE-Step and
  Kokoro are Apache-2.0; RIFE is MIT and Real-ESRGAN BSD-3; **FLUX.1 Kontext dev is
  non-commercial**, so a render that used it (`"consistency": "kontext"`) may not be monetised.
  Use `"consistency": "schnell"` for commercially usable output; the application flags the
  non-commercial path in its own interface.

## Model stack (v2, all local, all on the GPU)

| Stage | Model | Size | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Animate | Wan2.2 TI2V-5B GGUF Q4_K_M + UMT5 GGUF + Wan2.2 VAE | 8.5 GB | Apache-2.0 |
| Keyframes (default) | FLUX.1 schnell GGUF Q4_K_S + T5 GGUF + CLIP-L + VAE | 10.3 GB | Apache-2.0 |
| Keyframes (best consistency) | FLUX.1 Kontext dev GGUF Q4_K_M | 6.9 GB | Non-commercial |
| Music | ACE-Step v1 3.5B | 7.7 GB | Apache-2.0 |
| Smooth / sharpen | RIFE 4.9 · Real-ESRGAN x2plus | 0.09 GB | MIT · BSD-3 |
| Voice · word timing | Kokoro 82M · faster-whisper small.en | 0.6 GB | Apache-2.0 · MIT |
| Script work | Gemma 3 / 4B via Ollama | 3.2 GB | Gemma terms |

`scripts/setup_models.py` downloads this stack resumably and checks every file against an exact
byte size, and a sha256 where the catalogue has one, from a host-allowlisted catalogue.
`scripts/doctor.py` reports which device each stage will actually run on.

## Pipeline stages

The generation pipeline runs eight stages on a background worker thread, persisted in SQLite so
the queue survives restarts. The timings below are measured on an RTX 4060 Laptop (8 GB VRAM,
16 GB RAM).

1. **Narration and scene prompts** — Gemma 3 / 4B via Ollama rewrites the script into spoken
   narration and derives a visual prompt per scene (~10s each). If Ollama is unreachable or
   returns unusable JSON, prompts are built from whole sentences of the narration instead.
2. **Voice synthesis** — Kokoro TTS on the GPU, 8 voices (~5s per 100 words). XTTS v2 clones a
   voice from a reference clip.
3. **Character sheets and keyframes** — FLUX.1 in ComfyUI draws each character once, then draws
   every scene's first frame with that character in it. FLUX.1 schnell at 4 steps takes under a
   minute per keyframe; FLUX.1 Kontext dev at 20 steps takes 3–8 minutes each and gives the most
   consistent characters.
4. **Video clips** — Wan2.2 TI2V-5B GGUF animates each keyframe (image-to-video, 121 frames,
   480×832, 20 steps): about 6 minutes per scene. This is the slowest stage, and it sets the cost
   of a render.
5. **Frame smoothing** — RIFE 4.9 in ComfyUI, per clip, 24 → 48 fps (12–39s per clip, on by
   default). Optional Real-ESRGAN x2plus upscaling adds about 7 minutes per scene.
6. **Background music** — ACE-Step v1 3.5B on the GPU, mood-matched, side-chain ducked under the
   voice, mixed to −14 LUFS (optional, 34–40s for 79s of audio). MusicGen remains as a fallback
   only, because its weights are CC-BY-NC.
7. **Word-synced captions** — faster-whisper small.en on CUDA float16 times every spoken word, and
   the script's own words are burned in with the active word highlighted (optional, seconds for a
   whole film).
8. **Colour grade and mux** — FFmpeg curves, eq, film grain, dissolves and concat, encoded on
   NVENC (~50s).

The 13-scene sample story comes out as a 77-second, 1080×1920, 48 fps, stereo film at −13.7 LUFS.

## Rendering from a story file

`scripts/render_story.py` renders a JSON story file in seven resumable stages — `voice`, `refs`,
`keyframes`, `clips`, `smooth`, `music`, `edit` — each skipping files that already exist, so an
interrupted render continues where it stopped, and `--stage keyframes --only 8` redoes a single
scene. A story file carries a style, a cast of characters each with a description and a seed, a
consistency mode, a music prompt and seed, and one narration line plus one motion prompt per
scene, with an optional per-scene keyframe prompt and keyframe seed.

## Built-in style presets ("Skills")

A Skill is a JSON preset bundling voice, speed, scene pacing, aspect ratio, resolution, music mood
and an FFmpeg post-processing chain. Seven ship by default: Documentary (British male, slow, 16:9),
Explainer (American female, medium, 16:9), Product Showcase (American male, medium, 1:1), Cinematic
Story (British male, slow, 16:9), Social Short (American female, fast, 9:16, subtitles on),
Tutorial (American female, medium, 16:9) and News Brief (American male, fast, 16:9). Custom Skills
are JSON files in `app/skills/`.

## Architecture

Three tiers, each independently replaceable:

- **Electron frontend** — React 18, Vite, Zustand, Tailwind CSS. Project library, script editor,
  render panel, live VRAM meter, model and template browsers, batch modal.
- **Python backend daemon** — FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0, uvicorn. A persistent generation queue,
  VRAM-aware model lifecycle, a scene cache keyed on
  sha256(prompt+seed+model+resolution), 11 REST routes and one WebSocket progress stream.
- **Local model runtimes** — ComfyUI (Wan2.2, FLUX.1, RIFE, Real-ESRGAN), Ollama (Gemma) and
  FFmpeg, started lazily and only stopped if this application started them.

Heavy models run one at a time. The daemon unloads the LLM from Ollama before the video stage, and
checks free VRAM against the stage's requirement first; where there is not enough it warns rather
than silently substituting another video model, because v2 ships one video model and so has no
smaller one to fall back to.

Also included: reusable templates, automatic per-render version snapshots with restore, long-form
mode that chunks long scripts into 60–90 second sub-projects, XTTS v2 voice cloning from a
reference clip, and batch generation that queues up to 10 projects to render sequentially.

## Documentation

- [Project site](https://06pratyush.github.io/ai-video-pipeline/): a single page walking through
  all eight pipeline stages with the model and measured cost of each, the v2 model table with
  sizes and licences, the three-tier architecture, the built-in Skills, hardware requirements,
  install routes and an FAQ.
- [README](https://github.com/06pratyush/ai-video-pipeline/blob/main/README.md): what the project
  is, what changed in v2, the model table, the measured per-stage timings, install instructions,
  system requirements, quick start, the Skills and quality settings tables, architecture diagram,
  build-from-source steps, troubleshooting, future work and an FAQ.
- [CONTEXT.md](https://github.com/06pratyush/ai-video-pipeline/blob/main/CONTEXT.md): the system
  manifest — stack matrix, architectural rules, known shortcomings, and an append-only timeline of
  every change that reached main.

## Contributing and governance

- [Contributing guide](https://github.com/06pratyush/ai-video-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
  development setup, Python and TypeScript code style, how to add a Skill or a pipeline module,
  architecture conventions, and how to raise a pull request.
- [Review and merge policy](https://github.com/06pratyush/ai-video-pipeline/blob/main/REVIEW_AND_MERGE.md):
  how pull requests are reviewed, what blocks a merge, review comment severities, response times,
  the squash-merge rule and the release process.
- [Code of conduct](https://github.com/06pratyush/ai-video-pipeline/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [Security policy](https://github.com/06pratyush/ai-video-pipeline/blob/main/SECURITY.md): how to
  report a vulnerability, and the threat model of a localhost-only daemon with no authentication.
